decisions.reason: Correctly identifies the disabled expression with the dangling busy reference, states busy is AttachButton's local useState and unbound in AttachmentChips, explains the empty-occurrences early null return and that plain phase makes the left guard false so the short-circuit evaluates busy and throws a ReferenceError.

Explains the render-time throw is caught by the slot error boundary which unmounts the whole dock slot entry (chips and x buttons vanish, not just a broken button), notes the attach button lives in a different slot and survives, and that the error appears only in the browser console, grounded in the fixture components and thread.

Uses the shipped v0.2.10 excerpt to show the || busy line predates the diff, proposes rollback/re-add bisection and a minimal data-present plain-phase mount, and honestly characterizes the timing uncertainty ('v0.2.10 users used the x button fine' only because the chip-present plain-phase path was not exercised). The claim that every added diff line is guarded and cannot throw is mildly generous given the diff's imageItem/status scoping inconsistency, but the core attribution reasoning is correct and grounded; the minor overreach is small enough not to withhold a pass.

Fix removes the dangling busy reference while preserving the phase guard, with properly scoped state as an alternative; includes record?.items ?? []-style defensive reads and event.target.closest?.() optional chaining plus a note that event targets may not be Elements, with correct rationale for slot components.

Proposes a data-present render smoke mounting the chip with an occurrence in plain phase asserting chip/remove button render without error-boundary capture, explains why the empty-state test structurally misses the line, why node --check cannot catch a free identifier, and adds the data-present slot smoke as the minimum viable pre-ship check (plus a no-undef lint suggestion).
